summary:
SP is the category to fade across the board today. All three ratings are cold on starting pitcher — R1 at 40% (76-113, n=189), R2 identical at 40% (76-113), R3 slightly better but still bleeding at 43% (82-107) — and every single one carries a 3-game losing streak on that split. Meanwhile bullpen is the mirror image: R1, R2, and R3 all hot at +5.0pts, running 105-84 (56%) over the same 14-day window. If a play leans on SP grading strong but bullpen disagrees, discount it hard; if bullpen and SP both point the same direction today, trust bullpen's read over SP's.

Strong-play units tell a cautionary story short-term — R1 is flat at +0.0u over 14 days (43-50, 46%) and down -3.0u over the last week, R2 is bleeding -5.0u over 14 days, and R3 is the only rating still net positive lately at +2.0u (40-44) after a rough 7-day stretch. Season-long, R3 remains the top performer at +32.0u (54%, 127-109), narrowly ahead of R2's +25.0u and R1's +24.0u, so lean R3 when ratings split on a strong play. On category combos, trends+runs is the best agreement pair at 55.9% (199-157, n=356), with trends+bullpen right behind at 55.2% — a signal that pairs well with today's bullpen heat. Team-wise, ride BOS (76%, 25-8, strong 13-6 +7.0u) and TBR (73%, 22-8, strong 17-4 at +20.0u) hard when the model likes them; fade HOU strong plays, which are cratering at 22% (2-7, -8.0u) despite a respectable 58% overall mark — that gap between straight and strong grading on Houston is a red flag worth avoiding today.
